en.title: Leaning on the Everlasting Arms
en.author: Elisha A. Hoffman
stanzas:
What a [G]fellowship, what a [C]joy di[G]vine,
Leaning on the ever[A7]lasting [D]arms;
What a [G]blessedness, what a [C]peace is [G]mine,
Leaning on the ever[D7]lasting [G]arms.

Oh, how sweet to walk in this pilgrim way,
Leaning on the everlasting arms;
Oh, how bright the path grows from day to day,
Leaning on the everlasting arms.

What have I to dread, what have I to fear,
Leaning on the everlasting arms?
I have blessed peace with my Lord so near,
Leaning on the everlasting arms.
en.chorus:
[G]Leaning, [C]leaning,
[G]Safe and secure from [A7]all a[D7]larms;
[G]Leaning, [C]leaning,
Leaning on the ever[D7]lasting [G]arms.

notes: Three stanzas and refrain — the whole hymn; Timeless Truths and hymnary's representative text agree. Words Elisha A. Hoffman, music (and hymnary's tune name SHOWALTER) Anthony J. Showalter, both published 1887; Timeless Truths credits Showalter with the refrain's words as well. Meter as hymnary lists it (Timeless Truths writes 10.9.10.9.12.13, counting the refrain). Key: the hymnal key is A-flat (Timeless Truths score); G and A are each one semitone away and FORMAT's preference order picks G. Chords are Showalter's harmonization simplified, keeping the II7 (A7) approach into the mid-point half cadence in both stanza and refrain.
